newsitem.title: USA: Four journalists win Cabot prizes for Latam work.
newsitem.headline: Four journalists win Cabot prizes for Latam work.

text.p: Four journalists from Mexico, Costa Rica and the United States have won Columbia University's 1996 Maria Moors Cabot Prizes for their reporting on Latin American affairs, the university said on Thursday.

The winners are Dudley Althaus, Mexico City bureau chief for the Houston Chronicle; Ramon Alberto Garza Garcia, editor-in-chief of Reforma of Mexico City and El Norte of Monterrey, Mexico; Timothy Johnson, Bogota bureau chief of the Miami Herald; and Eduardo Ulibarri Bilbao, editor-in-chief and columnist of La Nacion of San Jose, Costa Rica.
The awards, in their 58th year, are the oldest in international journalism and were established in 1939 by the late Godfrey Lowell Cabot in memory of his wife.
